title: MILP Team
field: mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) solver engineering and computation: LP-based branch-and-bound and branch-and-cut as built into production and research MIP codes (presolve and probing, cutting-plane families and cut management, branching and node selection, primal heuristics, conflict analysis, symmetry handling, LP re-solves and warm starts inside the tree, parallel and deterministic search, numerics, tolerances and exact rational solving), decomposition (Benders, Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation and branch-and-price), and the measurement of solver progress on model libraries (MIPLIB, customer model sets, performance variability). Not yet represented by a voice of its own: polyhedral and cutting-plane theory, MIP and machine learning, symmetry theory and constraint programming. Mixed-integer nonlinear and global optimization belong to minlp-team; LP engine internals belong to lp-team
chase_hints: Optimization Online (optimization-online.org)
arXiv math.OC
ZIB-Report series (opus4.kobv.de/opus4-zib): MIPLIB and SCIP reports, and ZIB preprints by members (e.g. Bixby's SC 92-11 and Bixby and Martin's SC-95-45)
MIPLIB 2017 (miplib.zib.de) and its paper, Gleixner et al., Mathematical Programming Computation 13 (2021) 443-490, DOI 10.1007/s12532-020-00194-3, for the benchmark sets members measure on
COIN-OR open source (github.com/coin-or/Cbc, github.com/coin-or/Clp): cite code by repository, file and commit
Documenta Mathematica Extra Volume ISMP 2012 (Optimization Stories), e.g. Bixby, 'A Brief History of Linear and Mixed-Integer Programming Computation', pp. 107-121
Optima, the Mathematical Optimization Society newsletter (mathopt.zib.de/Optima-Issues/): interviews and solver histories
Hans Mittelmann's benchmark pages (plato.asu.edu/bench.html) for solver context only, never as a member's own words

card_dimensions.D3: problem class and data model: the MILP form handled (general integers, binaries, semi-continuous variables, SOS, indicator constraints, big-M), the model libraries and structures the technique relies on or exploits (MIPLIB versions, customer model sets, network, knapsack, set-partitioning structure), and the assumptions stated for any correctness argument
card_dimensions.D4: algorithm and implementation design: branch-and-bound and branch-and-cut components (presolve and probing, cutting-plane families with separation and cut management, branching-variable and node selection, primal heuristics, conflict analysis, symmetry handling, LP re-solves and warm starts inside the tree, parallel and deterministic search), decomposition (Benders, Dantzig-Wolfe, branch-and-price), numerical safeguards, tolerances and exact arithmetic, and any proof or invariant together with the device used
card_dimensions.D5: computational evaluation: test set (MIPLIB version, customer models), baselines (named solvers and versions), metrics (solved counts, shifted geometric mean time with its shift, nodes, gap closed, primal integral), time limits, hardware and thread counts, performance variability (seeds, permutations), and whether failures or slowdowns are reported
